title: Free solutions without finite boards
claim: Pre-registered 2026-11-10, before the proof attempt and before ticket B's census. For a nearest-neighbour shift of finite type X on the tree of F2: to be proved (1) a finite board exists iff the balance equations over X's tree patterns have a nonzero nonnegative solution; (2) Lemma A'': infinitely many pairwise disjoint half-trees with two completions each in one solution give a solution with trivial stabilizer; (3) L1: a vertex type that reaches a branching choice and recurs in two different child directions gives such a solution; (4) L2: a solution whose orientation (one neighbour one level lower) points to an end fixed by no nontrivial element is free; (5) the target W: every infinite X has a free solution, or the gap stated.
failure_conditions: A weakly aperiodic law with no solution of trivial stabilizer (against W).
A law certified by L1 or L2 whose solutions all have nontrivial stabilizers (against the certificates).
remaining_obligations: Targets 1 to 5, or the record of which fails and why
foundation_claim_scope: Boards made of identity distinctions on the names of the free group on two letters, under Leibniz's rule in full; finitary value laws over finite alphabets. Identity distinctions are distinctions of the law, never contact (A51).

validation.independence: Written by Claude in one session at the owner's go-ahead on 2026-11-10.
validation.status: pre-registered; the proof attempt to follow
